nodes.label: Do Not Put Effect Events in Dependency Arrays
nodes.norm_label: do not put effect events in dependency arrays
nodes.rationale: useEffectEvent deliberately returns an unstable identity that changes every render; listing it as a dependency therefore re-runs the effect on every render and trips the React Hooks lint rule. Depend on the reactive values (roomId) and call the Effect Event from inside the effect body instead.
nodes.source_location: ## Do Not Put Effect Events in Dependency Arrays

nodes.label: Store Event Handlers in Refs
nodes.rationale: Keeping the callback in a ref that a second effect keeps current lets the subscription effect depend only on the event name, so addEventListener/removeEventListener does not churn on every render. useEffectEvent is the cleaner modern equivalent of the same trick.

nodes.label: Initialize App Once, Not Per Mount
nodes.norm_label: initialize app once, not per mount
nodes.rationale: useEffect([]) is not once-per-app: Strict Mode runs it twice in dev and remounts re-run it. A module-level didInit guard (or init in the entry module) is what actually gives once-per-app-load semantics for things like loadFromStorage and checkAuthToken.
nodes.source_location: ## Initialize App Once, Not Per Mount

nodes.label: useEffectEvent for Stable Callback Refs
nodes.rationale: Reads the latest callback without listing it as a dependency, which avoids both the effect re-run (debounce timer restarted on every onSearch identity change) and the stale-closure bug the naive fix would introduce.

nodes.label: Deduplicate Global Event Listeners
nodes.rationale: A hook that adds its own window listener registers N listeners for N call sites; a module-level Map of key -> Set<callback> plus a single useSWRSubscription('global-keydown') collapses that to one listener that fans out to the registered callbacks.

nodes.label: Version and Minimize localStorage Data
nodes.rationale: A version suffix on the key (`userConfig:v2`) allows schema evolution with an explicit v1->v2 migration; storing only the fields the UI needs keeps tokens, PII and internal flags out of client storage. getItem/setItem must be wrapped in try/catch because they throw in private browsing, on quota exceeded, or when storage is disabled.

nodes.label: Use Passive Event Listeners for Scrolling Performance
nodes.norm_label: use passive event listeners for scrolling performance
nodes.rationale: Without `{ passive: true }` the browser must wait for the touch/wheel listener to finish before it knows whether preventDefault() was called, delaying scroll. Use it for tracking and logging; do not use it for custom swipe gestures or zoom controls that genuinely need preventDefault().
nodes.source_location: ## Use Passive Event Listeners for Scrolling Performance

nodes.label: Use SWR for Automatic Deduplication
nodes.rationale: A hand-rolled useEffect + fetch refetches once per component instance; keying on the URL through useSWR gives dedup, cache and revalidation for free, with useImmutableSWR for static data and useSWRMutation for writes.

nodes.label: React Compiler
nodes.rationale: Automatically hoists static JSX elements and optimizes component re-renders, which makes several manual memoization/hoisting rules redundant when it is enabled.

nodes.label: Avoid Layout Thrashing
nodes.rationale: Interleaving style writes with layout reads (offsetWidth, getBoundingClientRect, getComputedStyle) forces synchronous reflow. Batching writes then reading once, or grouping read and write phases, lets the browser coalesce style recalculation. Trade-off resolved in favor of CSS classes over inline styles because CSS files are browser-cached and classes keep separation of concerns. Impact MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Hoist RegExp Creation
nodes.rationale: Constructing a RegExp inside render recompiles it on every render; constant patterns go to module scope and query-dependent ones into useMemo keyed on the query (with escapeRegex). Caveat: a hoisted /g regex carries mutable lastIndex state, so successive .test() calls alternate results.

nodes.label: Animate SVG Wrapper Instead of SVG Element
nodes.norm_label: animate svg wrapper instead of svg element
nodes.rationale: Many browsers do not hardware-accelerate CSS3 animations applied directly to SVG elements; moving the animation class to a wrapping <div> lets the GPU composite transform/opacity/translate/scale/rotate. Impact LOW.

nodes.label: Hoist Static JSX Elements
nodes.rationale: JSX with no props or closure dependencies can be built once at module scope and reused instead of allocating a new element each render; the payoff is largest for big static SVG trees. Explicitly unnecessary when React Compiler is enabled, since the compiler hoists static JSX automatically. Impact LOW.

nodes.label: Combine Multiple Array Iterations
nodes.rationale: Successive .filter()/.map() chains each walk the whole array; a single for..of that pushes into several result arrays trades declarative style for one pass. Impact LOW-MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Early Return from Functions
nodes.rationale: Accumulating hasError/errorMessage flags keeps scanning after the answer is known; returning the failure result immediately skips the rest of the work and also removes mutable state. Impact LOW-MEDIUM. Example is a validateUsers() validator.

nodes.label: Use flatMap to Map and Filter in One Pass
nodes.norm_label: use flatmap to map and filter in one pass
nodes.rationale: .map().filter(Boolean) allocates an intermediate array and iterates twice; .flatMap() returning [] for rejected items does both in one pass with no intermediate allocation. Applies to conditional mapping, extraction of valid fields and parse-and-validate flows. Impact LOW-MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Early Length Check for Array Comparisons
nodes.norm_label: early length check for array comparisons
nodes.rationale: Arrays of different length cannot be equal, so an O(1) length guard precedes any expensive sort/join/deep-equality comparison. The rewritten hasChanges() also avoids allocating joined strings, avoids mutating the inputs by using toSorted(), and breaks on the first differing element. Impact MEDIUM-HIGH, greatest in hot paths such as event handlers and render loops.

nodes.label: Use Loop for Min/Max Instead of Sort
nodes.norm_label: use loop for min/max instead of sort
nodes.rationale: Sorting a copy just to read the first or last element is O(n log n) plus a copy; a single pass is O(n) with no allocation and handles oldest+newest at once. Math.min/Math.max with spread is accepted only for small arrays because the spread blows the argument limit (~124k elements in Chrome 143, ~638k in Safari 18). Impact LOW.

nodes.label: Use toSorted() Instead of sort() for Immutability
nodes.norm_label: use tosorted() instead of sort() for immutability
nodes.rationale: The concern is correctness, not speed: .sort() mutates in place, so sorting a prop inside useMemo mutates the caller's array, breaking React's read-only props/state model and producing stale-closure bugs. .toSorted() returns a new array (Chrome 110+, Safari 16+, Firefox 115+, Node 20+), with [...items].sort() as the older-runtime fallback. Sibling immutable methods: toReversed, toSpliced, with. Impact MEDIUM-HIGH.

nodes.label: Server Actions Are Public Endpoints
nodes.rationale: A 'use server' function is compiled into a public-facing endpoint; Next.js documentation states it must carry the same security considerations as an API route.

nodes.label: Fluid Compute Instance Reuse
nodes.rationale: Concurrent requests share one function instance, so in-process caches persist without external storage; this is what makes the LRU approach viable without Redis.

nodes.label: Automatic fetch Request Memoization
nodes.rationale: Next.js already dedupes same-URL/same-options fetch calls within a request, which is why React.cache() is reserved for non-fetch async work: DB queries, heavy computation, auth checks, filesystem reads.

nodes.label: Authenticate Server Actions Like API Routes
nodes.norm_label: authenticate server actions like api routes
nodes.rationale: Impact CRITICAL. Middleware, layout guards and page-level checks can all be bypassed because the action endpoint is callable directly, so authentication and authorization must live inside the action body. Prescribed order: validate input (zod), then authenticate the session, then authorize the specific resource, then mutate.

nodes.label: Cross-Request LRU Caching
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH. React.cache() dies with the request, so sequential user actions hitting different endpoints for the same data re-query; a module-level LRUCache with max size and TTL survives between requests. Trade-off is runtime-dependent: it only pays off where instances are reused (Fluid Compute), while isolated serverless invocations need Redis instead.

nodes.label: Per-Request Deduplication with React.cache()
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. Wrapping auth and DB reads in cache() collapses repeated calls across the component tree into one execution per request. Pitfall: lookup uses Object.is shallow equality, so inline object arguments never hit the cache - pass primitives or a stable reference.

nodes.rationale: In Next.js the framework Script component with strategy (afterInteractive / beforeInteractive) is preferred over raw script tags because the framework controls injection timing.

nodes.label: Use defer or async on Script Tags
nodes.norm_label: use defer or async on script tags
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH. A plain script tag blocks HTML parsing while it downloads and executes, delaying FCP and TTI. defer downloads in parallel and executes after parsing while preserving order (use for DOM/script-dependent code); async executes as soon as it is ready with no ordering guarantee (use for independent code such as analytics). Trade-off is ordering guarantees versus earliest execution.

nodes.label: Use after() for Non-Blocking Operations
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. Awaiting logging or analytics before returning adds their latency to every response even though the client does not need the result; after() schedules the work post-response. It still runs when the response fails or redirects, and works in Server Actions, Route Handlers and Server Components. Typical uses: analytics, audit logs, notifications, cache invalidation, cleanup.

nodes.label: Reference-Based Serialization Deduplication
nodes.rationale: Deduplication is recursive: string[]/number[]/boolean[] duplicate array plus every primitive (HIGH impact), while object[] duplicates only the array structure because nested objects dedupe by reference (LOW impact).

nodes.label: Avoid Duplicate Serialization in RSC Props
nodes.norm_label: avoid duplicate serialization in rsc props
nodes.rationale: Impact LOW. RSC to client serialization dedupes by object reference, not value, so derived props created with .toSorted()/.filter()/.map()/spread are new references and get serialized a second time. Doing transformations on the client keeps network payload minimal. Exception: pass derived data when the transformation is expensive or the client never needs the original.

nodes.label: Minimize Serialization at RSC Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH. Every property crossing the server/client boundary is serialized into the HTML response and subsequent RSC payloads, so passing a 50-field user object to a component that reads one field inflates page weight; pass only the fields the client actually uses.

nodes.label: Build Index Maps for Repeated Lookups

nodes.label: Use Set/Map for O(1) Lookups

nodes.label: Optimize SVG Precision
nodes.rationale: Impact LOW. Coordinate decimals beyond what the viewBox can resolve are wasted bytes; cutting precision to about one decimal shrinks the file with no visible difference. Optimal precision depends on viewBox size.

nodes.label: EXPLAIN ANALYZE for Diagnosing Slow Queries
nodes.norm_label: explain analyze for diagnosing slow queries
nodes.rationale: Guessing which index is missing wastes effort; EXPLAIN ANALYZE actually runs the query and reports real timings and buffer counts, so the bottleneck is observed rather than assumed.
nodes.source_location: ## Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to Diagnose Slow Queries

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements for Query Analysis
nodes.rationale: Without aggregated per-statement statistics there is no way to know which queries dominate database time; the extension ranks by total and mean execution time so optimization effort goes where it pays.

nodes.label: Autovacuum Scale-Factor Tuning for High-Churn Tables
nodes.norm_label: autovacuum scale-factor tuning for high-churn tables
nodes.rationale: Defaults (20% dead tuples to vacuum, 10% change to analyze) are too lax for busy tables; lowering the scale factors per table keeps statistics fresh where churn is highest without paying that cost everywhere.

nodes.label: Maintain Table Statistics with VACUUM and ANALYZE
nodes.norm_label: maintain table statistics with vacuum and analyze
nodes.rationale: The planner chooses strategies from statistics; stale statistics make a 1M-row table look like 1000 rows and yield a Seq Scan where an Index Scan would win. VACUUM reclaims space, ANALYZE refreshes the estimates.
nodes.source_location: ## Maintain Table Statistics with VACUUM and ANALYZE

nodes.label: Choosing the Right Index Type (B-tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, Hash)
nodes.norm_label: choosing the right index type (b-tree, gin, gist, brin, hash)
nodes.rationale: The default B-tree only accelerates ordering-based operators; containment, array, full-text, geometric and time-series access patterns each need a different access method, claimed as 10-100x improvement when matched correctly.
nodes.source_location: ## Choose the Right Index Type for Your Data

nodes.label: Index WHERE and JOIN Columns
nodes.rationale: Unindexed filter and join columns force sequential scans whose cost grows with the table, so the penalty compounds over time; rated CRITICAL at 100-1000x on large tables.
nodes.source_location: ## Add Indexes on WHERE and JOIN Columns

nodes.label: Partial Indexes for Consistently Filtered Queries
nodes.norm_label: partial indexes for consistently filtered queries
nodes.rationale: When every query carries the same predicate (deleted_at is null, status = 'pending'), indexing the excluded rows only costs storage and write amplification; a WHERE-scoped index is 5-20x smaller and speeds writes as well as reads.
nodes.source_location: ## Use Partial Indexes for Filtered Queries

nodes.label: Adding Constraints Safely in Migrations
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL has no ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS, so the obvious idempotent syntax is a hard syntax error (SQLSTATE 42601); wrapping the ALTER in a DO block that probes pg_constraint gives re-runnable migrations.

nodes.label: Index Foreign Key Columns
nodes.rationale: Postgres indexes the referenced primary key but never the referencing column, so both JOINs and ON DELETE CASCADE scan the child table in full and hold locks while doing it; an explicit index on the FK column is always required.

nodes.label: Partitioning Large Tables by Range
nodes.rationale: Beyond ~100M rows, both queries and maintenance touch everything: VACUUM takes hours and locks, DELETE of old data is unbearable. Range partitioning by time enables partition pruning and turns data expiry into an instant DROP TABLE.
nodes.source_location: ## Partition Large Tables for Better Performance

nodes.label: Principle of Least Privilege for Database Roles
nodes.norm_label: principle of least privilege for database roles
nodes.rationale: Granting ALL (or connecting as superuser) makes any SQL injection catastrophic; narrow per-table grants composed into nologin roles bound the blast radius and leave a readable audit of who may do what. Default PUBLIC access on schema public must be revoked explicitly.

nodes.label: Row Level Security for Multi-Tenant Data
nodes.norm_label: row level security for multi-tenant data
nodes.rationale: Filtering only in the application means one forgotten WHERE clause exposes every tenant's rows; RLS moves the predicate into the engine so the isolation holds no matter which client issues the query. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY extends it to table owners.
nodes.source_location: ## Enable Row Level Security for Multi-Tenant Data

nodes.label: Optimizing RLS Policies for Performance
nodes.rationale: A bare auth.uid() in a USING clause is evaluated once per row; wrapping it in a scalar subselect lets the planner evaluate and cache it once, claimed at 100x+ on large tables. Columns referenced by policies must also be indexed, since every query now carries that predicate.

nodes.label: SECURITY DEFINER Helper Functions for RLS
nodes.norm_label: security definer helper functions for rls
nodes.rationale: Running with the creator's privileges bypasses RLS on the tables the function reads, which is exactly what makes a membership lookup cheap and exactly what makes it dangerous: the trade-off is paid for with an explicit auth.uid() check inside the body, a non-exposed schema, and REVOKE EXECUTE from anon/authenticated/service_role.

nodes.label: Impact Level Scale (CRITICAL to LOW)
nodes.rationale: CRITICAL = 10-100x, HIGH = 5-20x, MEDIUM-HIGH = 2-5x, MEDIUM = 1.5-3x, LOW-MEDIUM = 1.2-2x, LOW = incremental; the scale ties a rule's declared impact to a measurable speedup band.

nodes.label: Transaction Mode vs Session Mode Pooling
nodes.norm_label: transaction mode vs session mode pooling
nodes.rationale: Transaction mode returns the connection after each transaction and suits most apps; session mode holds it for the whole session and is required for prepared statements and temp tables.

nodes.label: COPY for Bulk Loading
nodes.rationale: COPY (from file or stdin, CSV format) is the fastest path for large imports, beyond what multi-row INSERT achieves.

nodes.label: Vercel Fluid Compute
nodes.rationale: Concurrent requests share one function instance, so module-level caching survives across requests without cold-start penalties; in traditional serverless each cold start re-executes module scope and only warm invocations reuse it.

nodes.label: Writing Guidelines for Postgres References
nodes.rationale: Guidelines are shaped for LLM/agent consumption: concrete SQL rewrites over philosophical advice, semantic table/column names because names carry intent for LLMs, SQL-only by default for portability (application code only for pooling, transactions, ORM N+1 and prepared statements), and comments that explain why rather than what.

nodes.label: Postgres Rule Section Definitions
nodes.rationale: Rules are auto-assigned to categories by filename prefix (query, conn, security, schema, lock, data, monitor, advanced), so the filename itself is the taxonomy; each section carries its own impact band, e.g. conn and security CRITICAL, lock MEDIUM-HIGH, data MEDIUM, advanced LOW.

nodes.label: Postgres Reference Rule Template
nodes.rationale: Fixes the shape of every rule file: YAML frontmatter (title, impact, impactDescription, tags), a 1-2 sentence problem statement, an Incorrect SQL block, a Correct SQL block, optional trade-offs, and a reference link.

nodes.label: Error-First Structure (Incorrect then Correct)
nodes.rationale: Always show the problematic pattern before the solution because it trains agents to recognize anti-patterns.

nodes.label: Quantified Impact Requirement
nodes.rationale: Specific metrics ('10x faster queries', '50% smaller index') instead of 'faster' or 'better' let agents prioritize which fixes to apply first.

nodes.label: Configure Idle Connection Timeouts
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH, reclaims 30-50% of connection slots: with idle_in_transaction_session_timeout disabled, sessions sit idle in transaction for hours holding locks. Set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout='30s' and idle_session_timeout='10min', or server_idle_timeout/client_idle_timeout at the pgbouncer level for pooled connections.

nodes.label: Set Appropriate Connection Limits
nodes.rationale: Impact CRITICAL. Each connection costs 1-3MB RAM, so raising max_connections blindly (500 on 4GB) burns a gigabyte on connections alone and causes OOM under load; practical ceiling is 100-200, and work_mem * max_connections must stay under 25% of RAM.

nodes.label: Use Connection Pooling for All Applications
nodes.norm_label: use connection pooling for all applications
nodes.rationale: Impact CRITICAL, handles 10-100x more concurrent users: Postgres connections cost 1-3MB each, so one connection per request exhausts the database at a few hundred users. A pooler such as PgBouncer lets 500 users share ~10 real connections, sized as (CPU cores * 2) + spindle count.

nodes.label: Use Prepared Statements Correctly with Pooling
nodes.norm_label: use prepared statements correctly with pooling
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH. Named prepared statements are bound to one physical connection, so under transaction-mode pooling the next request lands on a different connection and fails with 'prepared statement does not exist'. Remedies: unnamed prepared statements (most ORM default), DEALLOCATE after use, or session-mode pooling (port 5432 vs 6543); drivers may need prepare:false (node-postgres) or prepareThreshold=0 (JDBC).

nodes.label: Batch INSERT Statements for Bulk Data
nodes.norm_label: batch insert statements for bulk data
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM, 10-50x faster: each single-row INSERT is its own transaction and round trip, so 1000 rows cost 1000 round trips; a multi-VALUES statement of up to ~1000 rows collapses that to one.

nodes.label: Eliminate N+1 Queries with Batch Loading
nodes.norm_label: eliminate n+1 queries with batch loading
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM-HIGH, 10-100x fewer round trips: a per-item query inside a loop turns 100 users into 101 round trips. Collect the IDs and use WHERE user_id = any($1::bigint[]) or a LEFT JOIN so it becomes one round trip.

nodes.label: Use UPSERT for Insert-or-Update Operations
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. SELECT-then-INSERT is a race: two concurrent requests both find nothing, both insert, one dies on duplicate key. INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE is a single atomic operation (with DO NOTHING as the insert-or-ignore variant) and can RETURNING the affected row.

nodes.label: Use Advisory Locks for Application-Level Locking
nodes.norm_label: use advisory locks for application-level locking
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. Creating dummy rows purely to SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on them adds a table and row-lock overhead; pg_advisory_lock / pg_advisory_xact_lock coordinate on a hashed name with no rows, transaction-scoped locks release on commit, and pg_try_advisory_lock returns immediately instead of blocking.

nodes.label: Prevent Deadlocks with Consistent Lock Ordering
nodes.norm_label: prevent deadlocks with consistent lock ordering
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM-HIGH. Deadlocks arise when two transactions take the same rows in opposite order; acquiring them up front with SELECT ... WHERE id IN (...) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE, or doing the whole change in one CASE-based UPDATE statement, makes the order deterministic. Observability: pg_stat_database.deadlocks, log_lock_waits, deadlock_timeout.

nodes.label: Keep Transactions Short to Reduce Lock Contention
nodes.norm_label: keep transactions short to reduce lock contention
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM-HIGH, 3-5x throughput and fewer deadlocks: holding SELECT ... FOR UPDATE across a 2-5 second external payment API call blocks every other query on that row. Do validation and network calls outside the transaction, guard the update with a status predicate, and cap runaways with statement_timeout.

nodes.label: Hoist Static I/O to Module Level
nodes.norm_label: hoist static i/o to module level
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH. Module-level code runs once on first import, not per request, so fonts, logos, config and templates are read once instead of on every invocation; awaiting module-level promises with Promise.all keeps the handler async-safe. Not for per-request/per-user assets, files that change at runtime, very large files (memory), or sensitive data that should not persist in memory.

nodes.label: Avoid Shared Module State for Request Data
nodes.norm_label: avoid shared module state for request data
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH. Server renders run concurrently in one process, so module scope is process-wide shared memory, not request-local: mutable module variables holding request data cause race conditions, cross-request contamination and security leaks between users. Safe exceptions are immutable static assets/config, correctly keyed cross-request caches, and singletons holding no request- or user-specific mutable data.

nodes.label: Parallel Data Fetching with Component Composition
nodes.norm_label: parallel data fetching with component composition
nodes.rationale: Impact CRITICAL. RSCs execute sequentially within a tree, so an await in a parent blocks its children; pushing each fetch into its own sibling component (or passing siblings through a children prop) lets them run simultaneously and eliminates server-side waterfalls.

nodes.label: Parallel Nested Data Fetching
nodes.rationale: Impact CRITICAL. Two sequential Promise.all stages make the slowest item of stage one gate every nested fetch; chaining the dependent fetch inside each item's own promise (getChat(id).then(chat => getUser(chat.author))) keeps one slow item from blocking the other 99.

nodes.label: Stale Closure Bug
nodes.rationale: A callback memoized with a missing dependency keeps capturing the initial state value forever; described here as the most common source of React closure bugs.

nodes.label: React Compiler Auto-Memoization
nodes.rationale: When enabled, the compiler optimizes re-renders automatically, so manual memo()/useMemo and some dependency-splitting become unnecessary; functional setState is still recommended for correctness.

nodes.label: Use useTransition Over Manual Loading States
nodes.norm_label: use usetransition over manual loading states
nodes.rationale: Impact LOW. A hand-rolled isLoading useState leaks on throw and adds a render per toggle; useTransition supplies isPending for free, resets correctly when the transition throws, keeps the UI responsive, and auto-cancels superseded transitions.

nodes.label: Defer State Reads to Usage Point
nodes.norm_label: defer state reads to usage point
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. Calling a subscription hook such as useSearchParams re-renders the component on every change even when the value is only consumed inside a callback; reading window.location.search on demand gets the same value with no subscription.

nodes.label: Narrow Effect Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Impact LOW. Depending on a whole object re-runs the effect on any field change; depend on the primitive actually read. For thresholds, compute the derived boolean outside the effect so it re-runs only on the boolean transition rather than on every continuous value.

nodes.label: Calculate Derived State During Rendering
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. Storing a computable value in state plus an effect costs an extra render pass and lets the stored copy drift from its sources. Derive during render; for resets on prop change prefer a key instead of setState in an effect. Cited source: React docs 'You Might Not Need an Effect'.

nodes.label: Subscribe to Derived State
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. Subscribing to a continuous source (useWindowWidth) re-renders on every pixel even though only the boolean matters; subscribing via useMediaQuery re-renders only when the breakpoint flips.

nodes.label: Use Functional setState Updates
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. Reading state directly forces it into the dependency array, so the callback is recreated on every change and re-renders memoized children; omitting it instead produces a stale closure. The updater form removes the dependency entirely, giving stable references and always-latest state. Direct updates stay fine for static values or values from props/arguments.

nodes.label: Use Lazy State Initialization
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. An inline initializer expression is evaluated on every render although React only uses it once; passing a function defers it to the first render. Worth it for storage reads, index/map building, DOM reads and heavy transforms; unnecessary for primitives, prop passthrough or cheap literals.

nodes.label: Extract to Memoized Components
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. Hooks cannot sit behind an early return, so a useMemo in the parent still runs during loading states; moving the expensive work into a memo() child lets the parent return the skeleton before the computation is ever reached.

nodes.label: Extract Default Non-primitive Parameter Value to a Constant
nodes.norm_label: extract default non-primitive parameter value to a constant
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. A default array/function/object literal in a memoized component's parameter list creates a fresh instance on every render, so memo's strict-equality comparison always fails and memoization is silently broken. Hoisting the default to a module constant (NOOP) restores it.

nodes.label: Put Interaction Logic in Event Handlers
nodes.norm_label: put interaction logic in event handlers
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. Modelling a user action as a boolean flag plus an effect drags unrelated values (context, theme) into the dependency array, so the side effect re-fires on changes that had nothing to do with the action. Running it in the handler keeps it once-per-interaction.

nodes.label: Don't Define Components Inside Components
nodes.rationale: Impact HIGH. A nested definition is a new component type each render, so React unmounts and remounts it, destroying state and DOM. Usually done to close over parent variables; pass props instead. Symptoms: inputs losing focus per keystroke, restarting animations, effects re-running every parent render, scroll position resetting.

nodes.label: Do Not Wrap Simple Primitive Expressions in useMemo
nodes.norm_label: do not wrap simple primitive expressions in usememo
nodes.rationale: Impact LOW-MEDIUM. For a couple of operators returning a boolean/number/string, the hook call plus dependency comparison costs more than recomputing, and primitives compare by value anyway so there is no identity to preserve.

nodes.label: Split Combined Hook Computations
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. One hook holding independent tasks takes the union of their dependencies, so any change reruns everything (changing sortOrder redoes filtering). Splitting lets each step recompute only on its own inputs, and chaining feeds the memoized intermediate into the next. Same applies to unrelated side effects in one useEffect.

nodes.label: Use Transitions for Non-Urgent Updates
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. High-frequency sources such as scroll handlers push a blocking render per event; wrapping the setState in startTransition marks it interruptible so urgent input keeps priority.

nodes.label: Use useDeferredValue for Expensive Derived Renders
nodes.norm_label: use usedeferredvalue for expensive derived renders
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. Deliberately letting the derived value lag lets React commit the keystroke first and compute the heavy result when idle; the query/deferredQuery mismatch gives a free staleness flag for dimming. Caveat: without useMemo keyed on the deferred value the expensive work still runs every render.

nodes.label: Use useRef for Transient Values
nodes.rationale: Impact MEDIUM. Mutating a ref does not schedule a render, so high-frequency values (mouse position, intervals, transient flags) belong in refs and the DOM node is written directly; reserve state for values the UI must re-render to reflect.

nodes.label: Section 2: Bundle Size Optimization (bundle)
nodes.rationale: CRITICAL because initial bundle size directly drives Time to Interactive and Largest Contentful Paint.

nodes.label: Section 1: Eliminating Waterfalls (async)
nodes.rationale: Ranked CRITICAL and placed first because each sequential await adds a full network latency round trip, so removing waterfalls yields the largest single gain.

nodes.label: better-all
nodes.rationale: Third-party library (shuding/better-all) whose `all({...})` object form lets each task await its siblings via `this.$.<name>`, so the scheduler derives the dependency graph and maximizes parallelism automatically.

nodes.label: experimental.optimizePackageImports
nodes.rationale: Next.js 13.5+ build-time transform that rewrites barrel imports to direct ones, keeping TypeScript types and autocomplete while removing the barrel cost; credited with 15-70% faster dev boot, 28% faster builds and 40% faster cold starts.

nodes.label: Prevent Waterfall Chains in API Routes
nodes.norm_label: prevent waterfall chains in api routes
nodes.rationale: In route handlers and Server Actions, kick off every independent operation immediately and await later: auth() and fetchConfig() have no dependency on each other, so serializing them costs a full extra round trip. Claimed 2-10x improvement.
nodes.source_location: ## Prevent Waterfall Chains in API Routes

nodes.label: Check Cheap Conditions Before Async Flags
nodes.norm_label: check cheap conditions before async flags
nodes.rationale: For `flag && cheapCondition`, evaluating the synchronous guard first removes the flag-service/network/DB cost entirely on the cold path. Explicitly framed as a specialization of Defer Await Until Needed. Trade-off noted: keep the original order when the cheap condition is actually expensive, depends on the flag, or side effects must run in a fixed order.
nodes.source_location: ## Check Cheap Conditions Before Async Flags

nodes.label: Defer Await Until Needed
nodes.rationale: Hoisted awaits block branches that never use the value; pushing the await into the branch that consumes it (and ordering early-return guards before expensive fetches) pays off most when the skipped branch is the common one or the deferred operation is expensive.

nodes.label: Dependency-Based Parallelization
nodes.rationale: Promise.all only handles fully independent work; with partial dependencies it forces a join that makes later tasks wait needlessly (profile waiting on config). better-all starts each task at the earliest possible moment. The dependency-free alternative is to create promises eagerly, chain with .then, and Promise.all at the end.

nodes.label: Promise.all() for Independent Operations
nodes.rationale: Three sequential awaits with no interdependency cost three round trips; Promise.all collapses them into one. Baseline CRITICAL rule of the waterfall section, claimed 2-10x improvement.

nodes.label: Strategic Suspense Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Awaiting data before returning JSX blocks the whole layout for data only one subtree needs; a Suspense boundary streams that subtree while sidebar/header/footer paint immediately. A promise started but not awaited can be shared across sibling components via use() so only one fetch occurs. Explicit trade-off: faster initial paint vs layout shift; skip it for layout-deciding data, SEO-critical above-the-fold content, and small fast queries.

nodes.label: Prefer Statically Analyzable Paths
nodes.rationale: Hiding a path inside a variable forces the bundler to include every possible file or widen Next.js output file tracing, costing larger server bundles, slower builds, worse cold starts and more memory. Same rule for import() specifiers and for fs paths built from process.cwd(): use an explicit map of import thunks, or make each final path literal at the callsite.

nodes.label: Avoid Barrel File Imports
nodes.rationale: Barrel entry points can re-export up to 10,000 modules, costing 200-800ms per import on every cold start. Tree-shaking does not rescue this: an external package cannot be optimized, and bundling it to enable tree-shaking makes builds much slower. Trade-off called out: deep direct imports break types for libraries like lucide-react that ship no .d.ts for subpaths, so optimizePackageImports is preferred where available.

nodes.label: Conditional Module Loading
nodes.rationale: Large data payloads are imported only once the feature is switched on; the `typeof window !== 'undefined'` guard keeps the module out of the SSR bundle, shrinking the server bundle and speeding the build.

nodes.label: Defer Non-Critical Third-Party Libraries
nodes.rationale: Analytics, logging and error tracking never block user interaction, so they belong behind next/dynamic with ssr:false and load after hydration instead of sitting in the initial bundle.

nodes.label: Dynamic Imports for Heavy Components
nodes.rationale: A heavy editor such as Monaco adds ~300KB to the main chunk if statically imported; next/dynamic with ssr:false defers it to on-demand load, directly improving TTI and LCP.

nodes.label: Preload Based on User Intent
nodes.rationale: Code-splitting trades bundle size for a load delay at click time; firing the dynamic import on hover/focus, or when a feature flag is on, buys back the perceived latency without putting the chunk in the initial bundle. Same `typeof window !== 'undefined'` guard keeps it out of the SSR bundle.

nodes.label: Choosing Appropriate Data Types
nodes.rationale: int overflows at 2.1 billion, varchar(n) adds an arbitrary limit with no performance gain over text, timestamp loses timezone, and float loses money precision. bigint/text/timestamptz/boolean/numeric cut storage ~50% and remove whole bug classes.

nodes.label: Lowercase snake_case Identifiers
nodes.rationale: Postgres folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase, so a quoted mixed-case name must be quoted forever; ORMs, GUI tools and AI assistants that drop the quotes then fail with 'relation does not exist'. A view can act as a compatibility layer when the casing is already baked in.

nodes.label: Primary Key Strategy (identity vs UUID)
nodes.rationale: Random UUIDv4 keys scatter inserts across the index and fragment it; bigint identity is sequential, 8 bytes and SQL-standard (preferred over serial). Distributed or externally exposed IDs should use a time-ordered form instead.

nodes.label: Cache Repeated Function Calls
nodes.rationale: A module-level Map is chosen over a React hook deliberately, so the cache works in utilities and event handlers and not only inside components. Single-value functions get a simpler nullable module variable plus an explicit invalidation hook (onAuthChange). Impact MEDIUM: avoids redundant computation such as slugify() running once per list item instead of once per unique key.

nodes.label: Cache Property Access in Loops
nodes.rationale: Deep property chains and arr.length re-evaluate on every loop iteration; hoisting them to locals turns 3 lookups x N iterations into 1 lookup total. Impact LOW-MEDIUM, applied only in hot paths.

nodes.label: Cache Storage API Calls
nodes.rationale: localStorage, sessionStorage and document.cookie are synchronous and expensive, so reads are memoized in a module-level Map (not a hook, so it works outside components). The cost of caching is staleness, accepted only with explicit invalidation: writes keep the cache in sync, the storage event deletes changed keys, and visibilitychange clears the whole cache when another tab or the server may have changed it. Impact LOW-MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Defer Non-Critical Work with requestIdleCallback
nodes.rationale: Analytics, recent-search persistence and prefetching block the main thread if run inline with a user interaction; scheduling them in idle periods keeps interactions and animations smooth. A timeout option bounds the delay for work that must still happen; large datasets are chunked against deadline.timeRemaining() in sub-50ms slices; setTimeout(cb, 1) is the fallback where requestIdleCallback is unsupported. Explicitly NOT for user-initiated feedback, awaited render updates or time-sensitive work. Impact MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Use Activity Component for Show/Hide
nodes.rationale: React's <Activity mode="visible|hidden"> keeps state and DOM alive for expensive subtrees that toggle often (dropdowns, menus), avoiding the re-mount cost and state loss of unmounting. Impact MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Use Explicit Conditional Rendering
nodes.rationale: JSX renders falsy numbers, so {count && <Badge/>} prints a literal 0 (or NaN) when the count is zero; an explicit ternary returning null makes the empty case render nothing. Impact LOW but it is a visible correctness bug.

nodes.label: CSS content-visibility for Long Lists
nodes.rationale: content-visibility: auto plus contain-intrinsic-size lets the browser skip layout and paint for off-screen list rows while preserving scrollbar geometry: for a 1000-message list about 990 items are skipped, roughly 10x faster initial render. Impact HIGH, and it needs no virtualization library.

nodes.label: Prevent Hydration Mismatch Without Flickering
nodes.rationale: Two failure modes are rejected: reading localStorage during render crashes SSR, and reading it in useEffect renders the default first and flashes. The accepted trade-off is an inline dangerouslySetInnerHTML script that runs synchronously before paint and writes the stored value onto the element by id, so the DOM is already correct when React hydrates. Applies to theme toggles, user preferences and auth state. Impact MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Suppress Expected Hydration Mismatches
nodes.rationale: Some server/client differences are intentional (random ids, dates, locale and timezone formatting); wrapping just that text in suppressHydrationWarning silences the noise. Bounded deliberately: it must not be used to hide real mismatches and should not be overused. Impact LOW-MEDIUM. Targets SSR frameworks such as Next.js.

nodes.label: Use React DOM Resource Hints
nodes.rationale: react-dom exposes prefetchDNS, preconnect, preload, preloadModule, preinit and preinitModule so the browser starts DNS/TCP/TLS and resource fetches early; calling them from server components begins the work before the client even receives the HTML. Each hint is matched to a case: prefetchDNS for later third-party domains, preconnect for immediate APIs/CDNs, preload for current-page critical fonts and styles, preloadModule for likely next navigation, preinit/preinitModule for code that must execute early. Impact HIGH.
